analysis:
Documentation-only change in docs/provider/cli-reference.md. The supplied units are base text at lines 2135-2521 (paths, provider.toml keys, LaunchAgent passthrough and runtime constants) and head text at lines 1-385 (header, GLM local qualification, cache, desktop, global options, subcommands, start, schedule and switch). None of these visible lines falls within the head changed ranges.

The file_changes map, marked complete, shows changes at head 743-769 and 1852-1860. Those lines document a new `darkbloom update --rollback` flag. It restores the retained predecessor and quarantines the installed release. It contacts no coordinator, cannot be combined with other flags, prompts unless `--yes` is given, and drains and restarts through the watchdog's journaled rollback under the update lease. These changed lines appear only in the truncated patch excerpt and are not in any supplied unit, so no citable regression exists.

Threat relevance: T-043 already records that watchdog rollback authority is the same replaceable provider binary. An operator-initiated downgrade to a retained predecessor bears on T-013/T-034/T-054: qualification and revocation of older signed builds must still be enforced coordinator-side via App Attest/legacy code identity. A rollback must not let a revoked or unqualified predecessor serve. That is backend-owned and outside the supplied evidence.

The interaction with the quarantine override (`--override-quarantine` now also reinstalls rolled-back releases) should be checked in UpdateRollback.swift and UpdateRecoveryState.swift.

The unchanged base text was examined (prefix-cache env passthrough relevant to T-041; add-on paths relevant to TB-012/TB-013). No changes were evident there.

Integration should verify the head lines 743-769 and 1852-1860 together with the rollback source.
